title: Insurance Claims and Policy Processing Clerks

tasks.short: Prepare claim documents, check completeness and obtain missing information.

steps.what: Retrieve claim documents and the policy record from the insurance case system.
Read supporting documents and enter facts into the insurance case system.

loop.input: Unstructured claim documents; structured submissions bypass the model.
loop.output: Claim fields with document references and unresolved fields.
loop.check: Validate field types, policy identifiers and dates; show source passages for clerk review.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; unresolved fields return to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Forms and mappings handle structured inputs; varied narratives and attachments still require reading.

steps.what: Prepare the claim form and supporting document list.
Check required fields, signatures and consistency against the policy record.
Contact the policyholder about missing facts and record their explanation.
Save the completed claim pack and pass it to the claims handler.

tasks.design: Configure the insurance case system in {OTHER} to retrieve records, populate forms in {DOCS}, check required evidence and route completed packs. A bounded extractor on {DATA_PLATFORM} handles varied attachments, with field review before posting; the clerk receives a missing-information checklist for policyholder conversations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document formats varied, required evidence differed by claim type, and records were poorly connected.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing form builders and validation rules cover much of the work. Bounded extraction handles remaining documents, while AI-assisted coding can shorten connector development.
tasks.still_hard: Missing evidence, contradictory accounts and unusual policy wording remain difficult. GDPR requires controlled access and a lawful basis, including applicable conditions for health data.
tasks.human_edge: Help distressed policyholders explain events and distinguish an absent document from an unclear account.

ambition.what: Assisted claim completion appointments for policyholders who struggle with digital forms

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time copying facts and more time resolving incomplete claims. They gain authority to offer assisted completion appointments within agreed service limits, not to decide coverage.

reach.task: Design an accessible document intake checklist.
reach.learn: Plain-language forms, alternative submission routes and document accessibility.

evidence.claim: Paperbox organises insurance emails and attachments into case files.
VKG has a documented case automating claims correspondence; it does not establish this task's savings.
Templates, required-field rules and a bounded extractor can support claim-pack preparation.

assumptions: The company processes insurance claims using an insurance case system represented by {OTHER}.
Shares and remaining-time estimates describe a typical task mix, not measured savings.
Document-heavy priors fit this task; clarification calls take more time than the weak mail prior suggests.
Build ranges cover a narrow pilot and may overlap; national consultation requirements vary.
unknowns: Claim types, required evidence and document languages.
Available templates, validation features and read/write access in {OTHER}.
Proportion of structured submissions and incomplete claims.
Applicable national rules, employee consultation requirements and health-data access conditions.
research_questions: Which completeness checks can existing configuration handle?
How accurately can extraction preserve facts and flag contradictions on representative documents?
new_work: Review extracted fields and unresolved completeness checks.
Maintain claim templates and evidence requirements.
Monitor access controls, extraction errors and connector failures.
Offer assisted completion appointments.
tasks.statement: Prepare insurance claim forms or related documents, and review them for completeness.

tasks.short: Calculate a proposed claim amount from evidence and policy terms.

steps.what: Retrieve the claim pack and policy terms from the insurance case system.
Read estimates and invoices, then enter loss amounts into the insurance case system.

loop.input: Repair estimates, supplier invoices and other loss evidence.
loop.output: Itemised amounts, currencies, tax fields and source references.
loop.check: Reconcile line items to totals; check duplicates, currencies and claim identifiers; review ambiguous amounts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; failed reconciliation returns to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured feeds use mappings; varied estimates and scanned evidence need document reading.

steps.what: Apply policy limits, deductibles and valuation rules to calculate the proposed amount.
Resolve disputed valuation or unclear policy treatment with the claims handler.
Record the calculation and its supporting explanation in the insurance case system.

tasks.design: Configure versioned calculation rules in the insurance case system in {OTHER}, using verified loss amounts and policy terms. A bounded extractor on {DATA_PLATFORM} reads residual documents from {DOCS}; unclear valuation goes to a claims handler, and the calculation remains a proposal until settlement approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Amounts arrived in documents, policy versions were difficult to map, and calculation tools did not explain exceptions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing calculation engines and validation rules already handle arithmetic. Better document extraction and faster connector development can close input gaps.
tasks.still_hard: Depreciation, causation, disputed repair scope and unusual policy terms need expertise. GDPR Article 22 conditions must be assessed before any solely automated decision with significant effects; this design does not automate refusals.
tasks.human_edge: Explain a disputed valuation and recognise when a technically correct formula gives an unsupported result.

ambition.what: Daily prioritisation of valuation exceptions by financial exposure and claimant delay

tasks.altitude: Routine arithmetic leaves the clerk's queue, while handlers spend more time on disputed evidence. The clerk can prioritise valuation referrals within agreed limits; settlement authority does not change.

reach.task: Analyse recurring valuation exceptions and propose rule improvements.
reach.learn: Exception sampling, financial exposure analysis and policy-version comparison.

evidence.claim: Shift Claims supports claims triage and automation of claims or parts of claims.
A documented motor-claims case automates eligible claims under restricted conditions; it does not establish general valuation coverage.
Claim arithmetic can use deterministic rules while disputed valuation remains with a handler.

assumptions: Routine calculations use {OTHER}; local spreadsheet workarounds are possible but not assumed.
The handler step represents exception time averaged across the task mix.
The judgement prior concerns valuation and policy interpretation, not arithmetic.
Estimates exclude rebuilding a full policy calculation engine; national consultation requirements vary.
unknowns: Existing calculation features and completeness of versioned policy rules.
Claim mix, valuation disputes and settlement authority limits.
Use of spreadsheets for unusual calculations.
Whether life or health pricing enters scope, triggering separate EU AI Act assessment.
research_questions: Which calculations can be configured without custom code?
Can historical cases be replayed with correct policy versions and explainable results?
new_work: Review ambiguous extracted amounts.
Maintain and test policy-version rules.
Investigate calculation differences and valuation exceptions.
Check rule changes against representative historical claims.
tasks.statement: Calculate amount of claim.

tasks.short: Match incoming information to a claim and attach it to the case file.

steps.what: Open incoming claim correspondence and download attachments from the shared mailbox.
Find the matching claim in the insurance case system.

loop.input: Correspondence without a valid structured claim reference.
loop.output: Candidate claim identifiers with source passages.
loop.check: Use exact references first; corroborate extracted identifiers against case records; never match by name alone.
loop.stop: One extraction attempt; multiple or uncorroborated matches enter a clerk queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Exact matching handles most references; identifiers embedded in free text require reading.

steps.what: Identify document type and check whether the file already exists.

loop.input: Documents without reliable type metadata.
loop.output: An allowed document category or unknown.
loop.check: Validate against the category list; compute exact duplicate hashes deterministically; preserve changed versions.
loop.stop: One classification attempt; unknown categories return to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sender rules and metadata cover standard documents; varied correspondence lacks consistent labels.

steps.what: Upload documents and metadata to the insurance case file.
Notify the claims handler that new evidence is available.

tasks.design: Connect {EMAIL} directly to the insurance case system in {OTHER} and {DOCS}, removing manual downloads and uploads. Exact identifiers and duplicate checks run first; bounded extraction and classification handle residual documents, while ambiguous matches wait for clerk resolution before attachment.
tasks.previous_blocker: The mailbox and case file were separate, references were inconsistent, and duplicate handling was weak.
tasks.enabler_now: Mailbox ingestion, case-system configuration and deterministic matching already exist. Small extraction loops can handle references buried in text.
tasks.still_hard: One email can concern several claims, and changed documents can resemble duplicates. Wrong-case attachment exposes personal data, so uncertain matches must remain unposted.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve ambiguous ownership and understand when a revised document changes the case.

ambition.what: Missing-evidence alerts for claims handlers before scheduled case reviews

tasks.altitude: The clerk works an ambiguity queue instead of moving files. They can correct document categories and case links within access limits, and flag missing evidence for handlers.

reach.task: Improve claim-file indexing and retention categories.
reach.learn: Document versioning, access boundaries and retention schedules.

evidence.claim: Paperbox organises insurance mail and attachments into case files.
VKG documents automation of claims correspondence and improved service-level compliance.
Exact references, duplicate hashes and idempotent attachment writes reduce manual filing.

assumptions: A shared mailbox is a material intake channel, so mail time exceeds the supplied weak prior.
Existing ingestion configuration supports attachments and receipt checks.
Ambiguous matches are resolved before the write step; routine exact matches need no separate approval.
This task shares intake components with claim preparation; savings must not be added twice.
unknowns: Current intake channels and share already attached automatically.
Case-system ingestion features, identifiers and attachment limits.
Frequency of multi-claim correspondence and revised documents.
Retention rules and applicable national employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: What proportion of documents can be matched using exact references alone?
Can attachment retries avoid duplicates while preserving document versions?
new_work: Resolve ambiguous case matches and unknown categories.
Correct attachment mistakes through an audited process.
Maintain sender mappings, category rules and retention settings.
Monitor ingestion failures and missing attachment receipts.
tasks.statement: Post or attach information to claim file.

tasks.short: Route approved claims for payment or investigation and confirm receipt.

steps.what: Open the claim pack and calculation in the insurance case system.
Approve settlement or select further investigation within delegated authority.
Prepare the payment instruction or investigation referral packet.
Send approved payment instructions to the finance system.
Send investigation referrals and permitted evidence to the assigned investigator.
Record transmission receipts and chase failed or unacknowledged handoffs.

tasks.design: Configure approval and referral templates in the insurance case system in {OTHER}, then send approved payment requests to {ERP} through a logged, duplicate-safe integration. Investigation referrals use an approved recipient and evidence list through {WORKFLOW}; handlers approve external disclosure, while receipts and timed exception alerts update the case.
tasks.previous_blocker: Approval evidence, payment records and investigation correspondence lived in separate systems, with manual checks for delivery.
tasks.enabler_now: Approval workflows and template generation are established capabilities. Deterministic connectors can carry approval identifiers, prevent duplicate requests and reconcile receipts.
tasks.still_hard: Recipient identity, changed bank details, disclosure scope and delegated authority remain sensitive. GDPR applies to referrals; national rules vary, and actual payment release remains a separate finance action.
tasks.human_edge: Choose proportionate investigation and challenge unsupported suspicion without treating a flag as proof.

ambition.what: Daily escalation of stalled payment and investigation handoffs by claimant impact

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time resolving failed handoffs and less time assembling packets. They gain authority to escalate stalled cases and request missing acknowledgements, while settlement and payment-release rights remain with their current owners.

reach.task: Coordinate investigation milestones and overdue handoffs.
reach.learn: Dependency tracking, escalation thresholds and sensitive-information sharing.

evidence.claim: Shift Claims supports claims triage and automation of parts of the claims process.
DNB's documented 2021 review found flagged claims reaching people in the six insurers reviewed.
Approval-linked requests, duplicate prevention and receipt reconciliation can automate transmission without automating settlement judgement.

assumptions: Payment and investigation are alternative branches; their shares represent an aggregate task mix.
Investigation may involve an external investigator, so disclosure has its own gate.
Sending to {ERP} creates a payment request, not a bank transfer.
Build ranges include access and applicable national consultation; individual productivity monitoring is outside scope.
unknowns: Current settlement limits, approval roles and payment-release controls.
Whether investigators are internal or external and which channels they accept.
Available receipts, retry behaviour and duplicate controls in {ERP} and {OTHER}.
Applicable national consultation requirements and permitted disclosure scope.
research_questions: Can every transmitted request be traced to a valid approval and acknowledged receipt?
Which referral fields and attachments require disclosure review?
new_work: Review external referral recipients and evidence scope.
Resolve failed transmissions and missing acknowledgements.
Maintain authority limits, routing rules and referral templates.
Reconcile payment requests and test duplicate prevention.
tasks.statement: Transmit claims for payment or further investigation.

tasks.short: Obtain missing information from policyholders and other people involved in a claim or application.

steps.what: Identify missing evidence in the {OTHER} insurance administration system.
Draft a specific information request in {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Missing information list, approved request template and contact preferences.
loop.output: A request explaining exactly which evidence is needed.
loop.check: Check required items, recipient, approved wording and absence of unrelated personal information.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; use the approved template if checks fail.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle routine requests; unusual evidence gaps need a short explanation in plain language.

steps.what: Check the recipient and send the information request through {EMAIL}.
Discuss unclear or sensitive information with the policyholder by phone.
Record responses and evidence in the {OTHER} insurance administration system.

loop.input: Written responses, attachments and clerk-authored call notes.
loop.output: Proposed evidence fields with source references and unresolved gaps.
loop.check: Validate field formats and source passages; distinguish customer statements from verified facts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per response; unresolved fields stay blank for review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured replies map directly; letters and call notes express the same facts in different ways.

tasks.design: Configure evidence checklists and reminders in the {OTHER} insurance administration system or {WORKFLOW}. A bounded drafting loop prepares requests in {EMAIL}; the clerk approves sending and handles sensitive calls through {TELEPHONY}. Reviewed responses update the evidence pack in {DOCS} and the case record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence requirements vary by claim type, and replies arrive across letters, attachments and calls.
tasks.enabler_now: Configurable checklists and inexpensive integrations cover routine gaps; bounded extraction and drafting handle the remaining free text.
tasks.still_hard: Identity checks, conflicting accounts, distress and inaccessible evidence still require personal contact. GDPR limits which information may be requested and shared.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise confusion or distress, ask proportionate follow-up questions and avoid treating an incomplete answer as an unwilling customer.

ambition.what: An assisted evidence appointment for policyholders who cannot complete written requests.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time composing reminders and copying replies. Within existing authority, they can choose an assisted appointment or escalate an evidence dispute; settlement authority does not expand.

reach.task: Plan assisted-contact appointments and balance callback capacity.
reach.learn: Queue forecasting, accessibility needs and escalation capacity.

evidence.claim: Paperbox organises insurance emails and attachments into case files; this supports intake feasibility, not autonomous customer conversations.
VKG reports automation of over 60% of claims correspondence; the result is a vendor case and is not a forecast here.
Rules, request templates and bounded drafting can reduce preparation while sensitive conversations remain human.

assumptions: The setting is a mid-size European insurer or insurance administrator with delegated clerical processing.
The {OTHER} slot denotes the insurance policy and claims administration system.
The supplied workflow list has no insurance claims workflow, so insurance case steps use other.
Time shares and remaining-time percentages are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Build ranges cover one initial claim type and include access review and any employee consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Available evidence checklists, contact permissions and secure submission channels.
Actual share of sensitive calls versus routine written follow-ups.
Access to case records and permitted processing of health information.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation arrangements.
research_questions: Which request wording produces complete replies without collecting unnecessary information?
How reliably can extraction distinguish a customer statement from independently verified evidence?
new_work: Review drafted requests and proposed evidence fields.
Handle failed deliveries, conflicting responses and overdue evidence.
Maintain checklists, templates and contact preferences.
Sample whether assisted-contact customers receive equivalent service.
tasks.statement: Contact insured or other involved persons to obtain missing information.

tasks.short: Check policy wording and claim facts to establish coverage or refer uncertain findings.

steps.what: Retrieve the applicable policy version from the {OTHER} insurance administration system.
Check dates, insured risks and limits in the {OTHER} insurance administration system.
Read exclusions and endorsements in {DOCS} against the incident evidence.

loop.input: Version-locked policy clauses, incident evidence and standard rule results.
loop.output: A draft comparison of disputed facts and relevant clauses, with citations and uncertainty.
loop.check: Verify every clause citation and factual reference; flag ambiguity and missing evidence without inferring coverage.
loop.stop: One comparison and one citation-repair attempt; conflicting or unsupported conclusions go to a handler.
loop.why_not_simpler: Approved rules handle standard conditions; unusual wording and factual ambiguity need contextual reading.

steps.what: Record findings and referrals in the {OTHER} insurance administration system.
Approve ambiguous or adverse findings in the {OTHER} insurance administration system.

tasks.design: The {OTHER} insurance administration system retrieves the effective policy version and applies approved coverage rules. A bounded reading loop compares exceptional wording and evidence from {DOCS}, then an artefact generator records the cited recommendation and referral. An authorised handler approves ambiguous or adverse findings before they become effective.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy versions, endorsements and incident facts were difficult to join reliably, and exceptional wording resisted fixed rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned rules cover standard conditions; source-linked reading can prepare the exceptional comparison at lower cost.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed facts, legal interpretation and outdated rule mappings remain expensive. Significant solely automated decisions need an Article 22 assessment, including applicable exceptions and safeguards; a later review offer alone does not establish lawfulness.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret ambiguity fairly, recognise when evidence is insufficient and explain a defensible coverage decision.

ambition.what: A daily review of unresolved coverage referrals before they delay the claim.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time investigating disputed facts and less time searching policy versions. They can prioritise referral preparation, while binding coverage authority stays within existing delegation.

reach.task: Analyse recurring coverage referrals and propose clearer decision paths.
reach.learn: Rule traceability, exception analysis and separation of policy ambiguity from missing evidence.

evidence.claim: Nationale-Nederlanden has documented rapid processing for some simple claims; this does not establish general coverage automation.
A vendor case reports automatic decisions for a restricted eligible motor-claims population, supporting narrow rule boundaries.
Article 22 requires assessing restrictions, exceptions and safeguards for significant solely automated decisions.
A cited reading aid can prepare exceptional coverage analysis without receiving decision authority.

assumptions: Standard checks use approved, versioned rules rather than model-generated coverage decisions.
The {OTHER} slot denotes the insurance policy and claims administration system.
Handler approval time is an average contribution across cases requiring referral.
Time shares and remaining-time percentages are hypotheses for a pilot.
Build ranges cover one policy family, including historical-version testing, access review and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Policy families, endorsement complexity and availability of historical wording.
Existing coverage rules and their approval history.
Clerical and handler decision limits.
Permitted automation under the organisation's legal assessment.
Whether any proposed use includes life or health risk assessment or pricing.

Can reviewers detect unsupported interpretations in a source-linked coverage comparison?
Which exception categories can be converted into approved deterministic rules?

Review exceptional comparisons and approve adverse findings.
Test historical policy versions and contradictory evidence.
Maintain decision traces and routes for human intervention and contest.
tasks.statement: Review insurance policy to determine coverage.

tasks.short: Validate incoming applications and claims, obtain required approvals, and create accurate insurance records.

steps.what: Sort applications, claim forms and attachments arriving through {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Incoming forms, email text and supporting documents.
loop.output: A classified intake pack with extracted fields and source locations.
loop.check: Validate schema, document counts, field formats and source evidence; quarantine unreadable or unsafe attachments.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; unresolved items enter the clerk's queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured forms map directly; variable attachments and free-text notices need bounded reading.

steps.what: Match the intake to customers and policies in the {OTHER} insurance administration system.
Check forms and supporting evidence in {DOCS} for completeness and consistency.
Resolve clerical exceptions in the {OTHER} insurance administration system.
Approve referred policy issuance using the supporting documents in {DOCS}.
Create the policy or claim record in the {OTHER} insurance administration system.
Send the approved policy documents or claim receipt through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: A reusable intake schema accepts structured submissions and uses bounded extraction for residual documents in {EMAIL} and {DOCS}. Rules match records, check completeness and route exceptions through {WORKFLOW}; approved instructions create records in the {OTHER} insurance administration system with duplicate prevention and an audit trail. Configured templates send policy documents or claim receipts only after the required processing authority is established.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mixed document formats, uncertain customer matches and fragile record interfaces made straight-through processing expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing validation features, reusable connectors and bounded extraction reduce the cost of joining intake to record creation.
tasks.still_hard: Issuing a policy can create contractual obligations. Reliable authorisation, identity matching, transaction recovery and special-category data controls need careful implementation; registering a claim does not approve settlement.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve contradictory evidence and recognise when a clerical correction would become an unauthorised insurance decision.

ambition.what: A pre-submission completeness check for broker-submitted applications.

tasks.altitude: The clerk manages exception queues and helps submitters fix recurring errors. They gain control over queue sequencing and completeness support within delegated limits, without acquiring underwriting or settlement rights.

reach.task: Specify insurance intake mappings and transaction acceptance criteria.
reach.learn: Field lineage, duplicate prevention, authorisation checks and recovery after partial failure.

evidence.claim: Paperbox supports organising insurance correspondence and attachments into cases.
PostNL offers scanning and conversion of physical business forms into data.
Shift Claims offers claims triage and automation; this establishes available capability, not suitability for every policy transaction.
Authorised record creation, duplicate checks and template notices can use deterministic workflows.

assumptions: The {OTHER} slot denotes the insurance policy and claims administration system.
Existing approval matrices distinguish claim registration, pre-authorised issuance and referred policy issuance.
The approval branch applies only when required; its time share is averaged across the task mix.
Routine posting and delivery require valid prior authority and verified recipient details.
Time shares and remaining-time percentages are pilot hypotheses.

unknowns: Current transaction interfaces, supported imports and existing configurable features.
Submission volumes, document languages and exception rates.
Which policy actions are already authorised before clerical processing.
Permitted recipient verification and delivery channels.
Applicable employee consultation requirements and access lead times.

Maintain field mappings, approval matrices and notice templates.
Reconcile submitted, posted and delivered transaction counts.
Investigate partial failures and sample completed records.
tasks.statement: Process and record new insurance policies and claims.

tasks.short: Enter, retrieve, organise and reconcile detailed insurance office records.

steps.what: Find requested records in the {OTHER} insurance administration system.
Copy insurance administration fields from {OTHER} into a tracking workbook in {SPREADSHEET}.
Name, link and file supporting documents in {DOCS}.
Resolve conflicting entries in the {OTHER} insurance administration system.
Apply archive categories and retention labels in {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Configure saved searches, case identifiers and document metadata in the {OTHER} insurance administration system and {DOCS}. Replace duplicate tracking in {SPREADSHEET} with a live records view, and use deterministic checks to prepare conflicts for the clerk. Retention labels follow approved schedules and legal holds, with exceptions routed through {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Disconnected search, inconsistent identifiers and local trackers created repeated entry and uncertainty about the authoritative record.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing search and metadata features often cover most of the task; small integrations can join identifiers and replace duplicate trackers.
tasks.still_hard: Historic duplicates, disputed corrections and missing source documents require investigation. Retention periods, legal holds and access restrictions need locally validated rules.
tasks.human_edge: Establish which source is authoritative and explain corrections without silently overwriting a contested history.

ambition.what: A permission-aware self-service case-document index for authorised office colleagues.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time locating and copying records and more time resolving conflicts. They can make documented clerical corrections within existing limits; disputed ownership and retention decisions remain escalations.

reach.task: Design a shared case index and maintain consistent record categories.
reach.learn: Metadata standards, permission-aware search, retention schedules and legal holds.

reach.task: Identify recurring causes of conflicting insurance records.
reach.learn: Data lineage and analysis of correction patterns.

evidence.claim: Saved searches, metadata, controlled updates and retention labels are established records-management capabilities.
Paperbox demonstrates insurance correspondence organisation, relevant to linking documents to cases.
The documented public-health spreadsheet failure illustrates the risk of relying on unchecked workbook capacity.

The {OTHER} slot denotes the insurance policy and claims administration system.
A local workbook duplicates fields already held in the authoritative record.
Source documents carry usable case identifiers; free-text indexing is not needed in the initial build.

Can a shared index preserve all existing document access restrictions?
Which conflict checks identify actionable discrepancies without overwhelming clerks?

Resolve conflict queues and document correction rationales.
Check archive exceptions and legal hold propagation.
Review permissions when roles or document categories change.

tasks.short: Explain claim procedures and provide suitable repair or contractor referrals.

steps.what: Read the policyholder's enquiry in {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Customer enquiry and allowed enquiry categories.
loop.output: Enquiry category and supporting text.
loop.check: Require an allowed category and matching source text; uncertain cases enter the clerk queue.
loop.stop: One classification attempt per enquiry; no automatic retry; ambiguity goes to a clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Unstructured enquiries describe the same need in many ways; structured submissions use rules instead.

steps.what: Verify identity in the insurance administration system {OTHER}.
Retrieve case context from the insurance administration system {OTHER}.
Find applicable claim instructions and approved referrals in {DOCS}.
Compose and send claim guidance or contractor referrals through {EMAIL}.
Explain sensitive or confusing cases by phone and agree next steps.
Record advice in the insurance administration system {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Configure a queue in {WORKFLOW} that links {EMAIL} enquiries to insurance administration records in {OTHER}; a bounded classifier handles free-text intent. Approved instructions and referral lists in {DOCS} populate response templates, with identity checks and clerk approval before disclosure. Sent messages and structured call notes return automatically to {OTHER}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy context, instructions and contractor lists sit apart. Clerks bridge them and interpret loosely written enquiries.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing queues and templates cover most of the flow. AI-assisted coding reduces connector effort, while a small classifier handles varied wording.
tasks.still_hard: Identity ambiguity, outdated contractor lists and questions that imply a coverage decision still need attention.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise distress, explain uncertainty and help customers choose practical next steps without promising cover.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from searching and copying to difficult calls and checking customer understanding. Coverage and referral decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Maintain a usable regional contractor directory.
reach.learn: Service-area mapping, directory ownership and referral-quality checks.

VKG reports automating over 60% of claims correspondence; this vendor case does not establish savings here.
Approved guidance can be selected by product, claim type and policy version, then inserted into templates.

The illustrated route is an email enquiry, with a phone conversation when needed.
Time shares and remaining percentages are design estimates, not measured results.
The configured guidance catalogue excludes coverage decisions and settlement commitments.

Check failed record links and sample sent guidance for accuracy.
tasks.statement: Provide customer service, such as limited instructions on proceeding with claims or referrals to auto repair facilities or local contractors.

tasks.short: Request missing information and inform policyholders or insurance agents about account status and approved changes.

steps.what: Check outstanding information and status in the insurance administration system {OTHER}.
Read replies and attachments in {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Reply, attachments and outstanding information checklist.
loop.output: Proposed checklist updates with source references and unresolved items.
loop.check: Check case identifiers, attachment references and field formats; a clerk approves ambiguous or material updates.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction attempt per reply; unresolved content goes to a clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Replies mix narrative, partial answers and scanned evidence; structured responses bypass the model.

steps.what: Draft an information request or status message in {EMAIL}.
Check the recipient and send correspondence through {EMAIL}.
Clarify incomplete or disputed information by phone.
Record correspondence and follow-up dates in the insurance administration system {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Configure information checklists and deadlines in {OTHER}, with {WORKFLOW} producing approved templates and sending routine correspondence through {EMAIL}. A bounded extractor proposes updates from replies; disputed or material content reaches a clerk before it changes the checklist. A scheduled queue identifies overdue cases, while delivery records and structured call outcomes update {OTHER}.
tasks.previous_blocker: The checklist, incoming replies and outgoing messages do not reliably update each other. Clerks remember what remains missing.
tasks.enabler_now: Template rules and delivery tracking already exist in many systems. Small integrations and bounded extraction can connect the remaining gaps.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting replies, insurance-agent authority, changed contact details and messages that carry legal consequences need careful handling.
tasks.human_edge: Ask a clear follow-up question when the customer cannot provide the expected evidence or disputes the record.

ambition.what: Daily escalation of cases stalled by missing evidence.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time chasing routine replies and reviews a daily list of stalled cases. Proposed delegated authority covers routing overdue cases to specialists, with coverage decisions retained by authorised handlers.

reach.task: Identify recurring causes of incomplete submissions.
reach.learn: Case-age analysis, reason coding and comparison of request wording.

evidence.claim: Paperbox handles insurer emails and attachments as organised case files.
VKG reports automation of over 60% of claims correspondence, supporting feasibility without establishing this task's savings.
Checklist triggers, approved templates, reminder limits and contact-history updates can use deterministic workflows.

assumptions: The specialist insurance administration system is represented by {OTHER}.

loop.check: Validate names, dates and amounts against records; preserve locked clauses; flag unsupported statements.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; unresolved facts or failed checks return to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard letters; unusual explanations need bounded drafting from case-specific free text.

steps.what: Review facts, tone and commitments, then approve the exact correspondence for sending.
Send approved correspondence and save a copy in the insurance administration system.

tasks.design: A case view in the {WORKFLOW} retrieves permitted facts from the insurance administration {OTHER} and approved templates from the {DOCS}. An artefact generator fills standard letters, with a bounded drafting loop for unusual explanations. The case handler approves the recipient and exact text before the {EMAIL} sends it and records delivery.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case facts and approved wording sit in separate places. Template maintenance and record links cost more than occasional manual drafting.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building record links and template generators. Bounded drafting can handle leftover narrative without deciding cover or settlement.
tasks.still_hard: Missing facts, disputed liability and wording that creates commitments still need experienced review. Reliable access to old correspondence can be expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a routine letter would confuse, distress or unfairly pressure the recipient, and choose a personal conversation.

ambition.what: An approved plain-language case timeline for policyholders with complex correspondence.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time assembling letters and more time resolving missing facts and preparing difficult explanations. Sending authority and settlement authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare an approval-ready briefing from correspondence and records.
reach.learn: Separate verified facts, open questions and commitments requiring approval.

evidence.claim: Insurance correspondence can be organised into case files automatically; this supports intake, not autonomous approval of letters.
Template generation, bounded drafting and the build ranges are proposed designs and estimates.
The digest reports an insurer case automating over 60% of claims correspondence; this is not a forecast for this task.

tasks.statement: Compose business correspondence for supervisors, managers, and professionals.

tasks.short: Calculate premiums, refunds, commissions, adjustments and reserves using approved insurance rates.

steps.what: Retrieve policy terms, transaction dates and amounts from the insurance administration system.
Select effective rate tables, commission agreements and reserve standards.
Calculate amounts in the insurance administration system, using worksheets for unsupported adjustments.
Check unusual results and obtain approval for amounts outside delegated limits.
Approve nonstandard rates, discretionary adjustments or reserve changes outside the clerk's authority.
Record authorised amounts in the insurance administration system and forward accounting entries.

tasks.design: Configure effective-dated rates in the insurance administration {OTHER}, then add deterministic calculations only for unsupported adjustments. A controlled integration sends authorised entries to the {ERP}, with reconciliations and an explanation of every amount. The {WORKFLOW} routes discretionary rates and reserve changes to an authorised specialist before posting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Core calculations often already exist. Remaining work involves fragmented rate versions, unusual adjustments and gaps between policy records and accounting.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes narrow calculation modules, regression fixtures and reconciliation links cheaper to build. The arithmetic and approval limits remain explicit rules.
tasks.still_hard: Reserve judgement, retroactive changes and ambiguous agreements need specialist interpretation. Life and health pricing needs assessment under EU AI Act Annex III 5(c); that classification does not automatically extend to all claims processing.
tasks.human_edge: Spot when the selected assumptions produce an implausible result and distinguish a data error from a genuine change in risk.

ambition.what: A weekly review of refund and commission anomalies by product and intermediary.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more of the week investigating unusual adjustments and explaining their causes. Specialist pricing, reserving and payment approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Investigate recurring financial adjustment anomalies.
reach.learn: Use reconciled populations, comparable rates and clear explanations of variance.

evidence.claim: Effective-dated rules and deterministic arithmetic can support routine insurance calculations; the proposed time savings are estimates.
EU AI Act Annex III 5(c) covers specified AI uses for life and health insurance risk assessment and pricing.
A documented insurer case processes selected simple claims rapidly; it does not establish automation rates for premiums or reserves.

The insurance administration {OTHER} supports the main product calculations.
Routine rule-compliant entries may post under existing delegated authority; exceptions require s5 approval.

tasks.statement: Calculate premiums, refunds, commissions, adjustments, or new reserve requirements, using insurance rate standards.

tasks.short: Enter policy and claim information, check it and resolve incomplete records.

steps.what: Open submitted forms and attachments, then match them to an insurance administration case.
Read submitted documents and enter fields into the insurance administration system.

loop.input: Unstructured forms and attachments remaining after structured field import.
loop.output: Provisional case fields with source locations and explicit missing values.
loop.check: Check field types, required values and identifiers; compare critical values with existing records.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; ambiguous identities, unsupported values and failed checks enter a review queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured imports remove most keying; varied scans and narrative attachments still need document reading.

steps.what: Check completeness, duplicates and inconsistencies against existing insurance administration records.
Ask the policyholder to clarify missing or conflicting information.
Confirm corrections and save the completed record in the insurance administration system.

tasks.design: Replace re-keying with structured capture in the {WORKFLOW} and validated imports into the insurance administration {OTHER}. A bounded extraction loop reads leftover documents from the {DOCS}, while deterministic checks detect missing fields, duplicates and conflicts. Only uncertain or consequential corrections require clerk approval; the clerk keeps difficult clarification calls.
tasks.previous_blocker: External submissions arrive in inconsistent formats. Legacy record interfaces and unclear field ownership make reliable imports costly.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured forms and imports already remove much keying. AI-assisted coding and bounded extraction reduce the cost of handling remaining document formats.
tasks.still_hard: Identity ambiguity, contradictory documents and health information need careful handling. Passing format checks does not prove that a submitted fact is true.
tasks.human_edge: Help a policyholder explain an unusual situation without forcing it into an incorrect field or losing important context.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time copying fields and more time resolving incomplete or contradictory submissions. Record-correction rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Specify field mappings and exception routes between intake and records.
reach.learn: Define source ownership, duplicate protection and recoverable write failures.

reach.task: Resolve document-to-record mismatches.
reach.learn: Use source evidence and distinguish a missing value from an inferred value.

evidence.claim: Insurance mailroom software organises emails and attachments into case files.
Business-post services can scan documents and turn forms into data.

tasks.statement: Enter insurance- and claims-related information into database systems.

tasks.short: Process requested changes to beneficiaries, cover and insurance type, then update records and confirmations.

steps.what: Read the change request and retrieve the policy in the insurance administration system.

loop.input: Free-text change request and supporting documents linked to a policy.
loop.output: Proposed change fields, requested effective date and supporting source locations.
loop.check: Validate policy identifiers and allowed field names; flag ambiguous people, dates and requested cover.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; unresolved ambiguity returns to the clerk without changing the policy.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured change forms need no model; letters can express several changes without consistent labels.

steps.what: Verify requester authority, supporting evidence and contractual eligibility for the change.
Calculate the premium adjustment and identify effects on open claims.
Approve consequential beneficiary, cover or product changes and resolve nonstandard requests.
Apply approved changes and effective dates in the insurance administration system.
Generate the endorsement, check its details and send the change confirmation.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} captures change requests and presents a proposed difference against the insurance administration {OTHER}; a bounded loop reads free-text requests only. Deterministic eligibility checks and the shared calculation service prepare an impact summary before the authorised handler approves consequential changes. An integration applies the approved version, and a template generator in the {DOCS} prepares the endorsement for checked delivery through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests mix informal wording with legally important instructions. Effective dates, authority checks and downstream claim effects cross several records and teams.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes difference views, version checks and integrations cheaper. Bounded extraction can structure requests while leaving eligibility and authorisation explicit.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed authority, beneficiary ambiguity, retroactive cover and changes affecting open claims remain difficult. GDPR Article 22 needs assessment where solely automated decisions have legal or similarly significant effects; national insurance and employment rules also vary.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise coercion, unclear intent or an apparently simple change that could remove protection, then secure informed clarification.

ambition.what: A provisional change-impact preview showing premium, effective date and cover differences before commitment.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time clarifying intent and explaining consequences, with less repeated record editing. The clerk can prepare previews but gains no independent underwriting or beneficiary-approval authority.

reach.task: Design checks for high-consequence record changes.
reach.learn: Use version control, approval evidence and downstream reconciliation to prevent silent inconsistencies.

reach.task: Coordinate exception routing and service handoffs.
reach.learn: Define escalation paths and measure unresolved cases without ranking individual clerks.

GDPR Article 22 restricts specified solely automated decisions and provides safeguards where applicable.
Dutch works-council rules can require consent for employee-monitoring arrangements; applicability elsewhere depends on national rules.

tasks.short: Maintain complete policyholder files and record approved policy changes, cancellations and reinstatements.

steps.what: Gather incoming policy documents and related correspondence.
Find the policyholder file in the {OTHER} policy administration system.

loop.input: Document bundle and permitted policyholder lookup fields.
loop.output: Source-linked identifiers and a proposed record match.
loop.check: Use exact identifiers first. Require consistent identifying fields; ambiguous matches enter a review queue.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; missing, conflicting or ambiguous identifiers go to a clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured identifiers use rules; scanned letters and free-text correspondence need extraction.

steps.what: Compare documents with existing records and check completeness, dates and requested changes.
Resolve missing information or conflicting instructions with the policyholder or representative.
Enter proposed changes in the {OTHER} policy administration system.
Approve cancellations, reinstatements and exceptions requiring delegated authority.
Apply authorised changes and verify the saved policy status.
File supporting documents under the correct policyholder and retention category.

tasks.design: Configure intake from {EMAIL} into {DOCS}, with a queue in {WORKFLOW} linked to the {OTHER} policy administration system. A service on {DATA_PLATFORM} uses exact identifiers first, bounded extraction for remaining documents, and deterministic checks to prepare record changes. Existing approval controls govern consequential changes; authorised updates write back to {OTHER}, verify the saved result and archive supporting documents in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documents arrive in varied formats, identifiers are incomplete, and file stores do not consistently connect to policy records. Approval rules and legacy interfaces make unattended updates expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing intake and approval configuration can cover much of the flow. AI-assisted coding reduces connector development effort, while bounded extraction handles residual documents without delegating policy decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Identity ambiguity, conflicting instructions, historical records and effective dates remain difficult. GDPR applies, including Article 22 where decisions have significant effects; EU AI Act duties depend on the actual use. National consultation rules and retention requirements need local assessment.
tasks.human_edge: A clerk can recognise disputed authority, understand a policyholder's circumstances and resolve contradictory instructions. A supervisor remains accountable for consequential exceptions.

ambition.what: Pre-renewal file readiness checks that identify missing reinstatement evidence before the renewal deadline.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more of the week resolving incomplete or disputed files and coordinating renewal readiness. They can prioritise remediation within agreed service limits; cancellation and reinstatement authority does not automatically expand.

reach.learn: Queue ageing, arrival patterns and service-level capacity planning.

reach.learn: Field mapping, effective-date rules, access controls and reconciliation.
